user.title: Pair a Deskmate device
user.description:
Home Assistant will generate a pairing code. Paste it into Deskmate (first-run screen or Settings -> Deskmate integration) on the computer you want to pair. The code carries the key and this Home Assistant's address, so there is nothing else to type. The entry binds itself to the first computer that authenticates with it.

If an entry is already waiting for pairing, its code is shown again instead of creating another one.

show_key.title: Pairing code
show_key.description:
Copy this pairing code into Deskmate:

`{code}`

Older Deskmate versions take only the bare key:

`{key}`

Update this integration before Deskmate on the computer. Deskmate 0.6 speaks protocol v2 only.

new_key.title: New pairing code
new_key.description:
The old key stops working as soon as you confirm. Copy the new pairing code into Deskmate:

`{code}`

Bare key for older Deskmate versions:

`{key}`

unbind.title: Unbind this entry
unbind.description: Currently bound to `{node_id}`. After unbinding, the entry attaches to the next computer that authenticates with its pairing key. Entities and their history are kept.

cascade_on.title: Enable cascade encryption
cascade_on.description:
Adds a second encryption layer: ChaCha20-Poly1305 wrapped around AES-256-GCM, with its own key. It only helps if one of the two ciphers is ever broken. Both keys are stored in the same places (here and in Deskmate), so it does not help if a key is stolen. Protocol v2 already derives fresh session keys from an ephemeral X25519 exchange.

Both sides must have it on. Paste this key into Deskmate under Geeky stuff, then confirm here. The connection drops until both ends match. It is shown only once:

`{key}`

cascade_off.title: Disable cascade encryption
cascade_off.description: Traffic goes back to a single AES-256-GCM layer. Turn it off in Deskmate as well, otherwise that computer will not reconnect.

add_user.title: Pair another Windows user
add_user.description:
For a computer that several people use with their own Windows accounts. Install Deskmate on the other account and paste this code there:

`{code}`

That account then reports as `{node_id}`: the same device, the same entities. Only one account is connected at a time, the one someone is using right now; when you switch users, the connection moves over.

The code contains this computer's pairing key. Do not share it outside this computer. To revoke every account at once, generate a new pairing key.

menu_options.add_user: Pair another Windows user on this computer

abort.pending_reused: An entry is already waiting for pairing. Its code was shown again - nothing new was created.
abort.add_user_done: Done. Paste the code into Deskmate on the other Windows account.

unknown_node.title: Deskmate: an unpaired computer keeps connecting
unknown_node.description:
A computer calling itself `{node}` ({ip}) keeps failing the Deskmate handshake. No paired entry matches that name, or its pairing key is different.

Either pair it (Add integration -> Deskmate, then paste the key into Deskmate), or - if it should use an entry that already exists - open that entry, choose Reconfigure -> Unbind from the current computer, and let it re-attach.
